title: Three distinct authority questions
summary: Authentication attribution, Access Control, and Permissions are deliberately separate. Authentication proves who produced evidence and grants no authority; Access Control decides whether a principal may cross a protected domain boundary; Permissions decides whether that principal may invoke an exact method on an exact object after Security Effect evaluation.
invariants: Authentication attribution is provenance/integrity only; it is not permission to log on, enter a domain, or call a method.
Access Control is coarse domain admission: permission to enter the building.
Permissions is exact subject x object x method authority evaluated after Security Effect.
Passing Access Control never implies method Permission.

provenance.claim: The project separates authentication attribution, Access Control domain entry, exact method/object Permissions, and leaves Alchemy Security Manager as enforcement point.
